 Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Josh Turek speaks Oct. 11, 2026, during the annual Democratic Fish Fry fundraiser in Des Moines.
 USA Today Network 
 Iowa voters have the opportunity to send a new voice to the U.S. Senate this fall, filling an open seat for the first time since 2014.
 Candidates include Republican U.S. Rep. Ashley Hinson, Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek and Libertarian Thomas Laehn.
 We believe that new Senate voice should be Turek’s.
 Turek, who lives in Council Bluffs, is an inspiring candidate to say the least. He was born with spina bifida, a congenital birth defect related to his father’s exposure to the chemical defoliant Agent Orange while he served in Vietnam.
 Turek had 21 surgeries to address his condition before age 12. He grew up in a large family that struggled at times to make ends meet. He was bullied by kids at school due to his disability. But in seventh grade, Turek started playing wheelchair basketball. The sport would lead him to a brilliant career at Southwestern Minnesota University, where he was the team’s top scorer and was a four-year All-American.
 Turek played basketball in countries around the world. He came back to the U.S. and became a member of the U.S. National Team, which won a bronze medal in the 2012 Paralympics and won two gold medals at the games in Rio de Janeiro and Tokyo.
 Turek decided to compete for an Iowa House seat, which meant crawling up steps carrying his wheelchair to knock doors at voters’ homes. He initially won by just six votes, but won by 5 percentage points in 2024 while President Donald Trump won the district by 8 points.
 He met his wife while playing basketball in Spain and became fluent in Spanish. She is now a naturalized U.S. citizen. He’s still crawling up steps to meet voters in his Senate campaign.
 “I’ve got to tell you, Josh Turek has a real grit,” said former U.S. Sen. Tom Harkin, according to the Iowa Capital Dispatch , as he campaigned Sunday with Turek. “He’ll outwork you. He’ll outwork any candidate. He’ll out-campaign you. And all of the time, keeping his sense of who he is and what he believes in and what he supports.”
 A Turek win would return the balance we once had with GOP Sen. Chuck Grassley and Harkin representing Iowa.
 Turek’s story helps him better understand the needs of struggling Iowans, kids who face bullying because of who they are, disabled people who depend on Medicaid and other safety net programs, and immigrants who come to the U.S. hoping to become Americans.
 Hinson and her allies have focused attacks on the fact Turek missed more than half the floor votes in the Iowa House while he campaigned for Senate. But trying to label Turek as a “lazy liberal,” after a lifetime of difficult climbs, strikes us as a lazy GOP attack.
 It’s unfortunate Turek couldn’t get to Washington and start voting sooner.
 Turek wouldn’t have voted in favor of the Big Beautiful Bill Act, which cut Medicaid by $1 trillion, including a $900 million annual reduction in Iowa funding that could lead anywhere from 60,000 to 100,000 Iowans to lose coverage. Other provisions could leave 24,000 Iowans without food assistance. Hinson enthusiastically voted yes.
 Turek would have voted to extend subsidies to help cover the cost of rising premiums. Hinson did not support the extension, and 21,000 Iowans have lost coverage.
 Hinson entered the Senate race proclaiming her desire to become Trump’s strongest ally in the Senate. She voted against impeaching Trump after the Jan. 6, 2021, riot and opposed the creation of a committee to investigate the storming of the Capitol. She gladly accepted his endorsement again and again and has supported some of his most destructive policies, including tariffs and the war in Iran, which have spawned dire economic consequences.
 Now that Trump’s popularity has hit new lows, Hinson has sought to distance herself from the president’s harmful actions. But after years of loyalty to Trump, it’s too late.
 We need a Congress that will stand up to Trump’s worst excesses. Turek would be part of it.
 Turek would seek to roll back Medicaid cuts and expand subsidies for Affordable Care Act premiums. He also would expand Medicare’s ability to negotiate for lower prescription drug prices and cap drug costs. He would prohibit health insurers from denying medically necessary care for cancer patients.
 Hinson has claimed Turek wants to give taxpayer-funded benefits to undocumented immigrants, which is already illegal under federal law. She also contends Turek supports “sex changes for kids,” which is a distortion of his voting record.
 It’s been a sharply divisive and incredibly expensive campaign. According to Quiver Analytics, Republicans, Democrats and allied groups have spent $182 million trying to win Iowa’s Senate seat, which could decide partisan control of the Senate.
 Turek hasn’t had to reinvent himself to become a contender. The contest, currently, is agonizingly close. We urge Iowans to help Turek make that climb.
